executiveSummary: GM0392 is identity-correct, geographically coherent, deterministic and numerically complete across the nine individual hazards plus compound, six checkpoints and eight services, but it is not locally calibrated enough for operational first-72-hour use. Seven unrelated nonzero individual hazards reuse exactly one complete 111-neighbourhood order, led by Romolenpolder-west with only 25 residents. A controlled earthquake at the municipal centre ranks its containing Burgwal neighbourhood 99th, and a controlled fire source at the Haarlemmerhout neighbourhood centre ranks Haarlemmerhout 97th. The coastal preset produces legacy internal flood amplitude 2.129932, rendered as 100% inundation stress, with 99,044 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without a selected coastal/Noordzeekanaal/Spaarne hydraulic event or defence state; meanwhile the exact-zero major-river result does not cover Rijnland boezem, regional-kade, Spaarne or pluvial pathways. Public data strongly supports mechanism-specific context and NoData, but not live utility topology, route/bridge state, care acceptance, resources or recovery. Desktop and mobile work without overflow and disclose generic evidence classes, yet exact Haarlem outputs lack an adjacent municipality-specific causal warning.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0392 official 2025 statistics, full and generalized administrative geography, BAG places and BRT settlements
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; PDOK services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK source identifies GM0392 as Haarlem and reports 168,743 residents, density 5,776 per square kilometre, 17.6% aged 65 or older and 35,803 one-person households. The 2025 full feature is a one-component, one-ring MultiPolygon with 1,654 vertices; its generalized source has 95 vertices and preserves the MultiPolygon type.

The generated centre [4.6434227866612225, 52.378977360728854] and BAG label points for Haarlem and Spaarndam gem. Haarlem fall inside the generalized boundary. BAG is daily, Public Domain Mark 1.0 point/place context; BRT TOP10NL is CC BY 4.0, scale/feature-actuality dependent, and returns Haarlem woonkern and Zuid Schalkwijk deelkern.

The 111 published neighbourhood rows sum to 168,770 residents, 27 above the official municipality total (+0.016%); deterministic allocation reconciles to 168,743. CBS small-area values can be rounded, suppressed, unavailable or not applicable. Null and missing fields remain NoData, never zero population, zero vulnerability or safe conditions.

Annual administrative/statistical coverage is not event-time occupancy. Visitors, commuters, patients, students registered elsewhere, responders, household stocks and facility demand are outside these resident totals.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Kennemerland 2023–2030 and Regionaal Crisisplan 2026–2030
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile adopted 10 July 2023 for 2023–2030; crisis plan version 1.0 adopted 20 November 2025 for 2026–2030
supports: The profile explicitly covers overstroming, nature fire, extreme weather, drought/heat, power/gas/drinking-water/ICT interruption, land/water/rail/tunnel incidents and hazardous substances. It identifies lower polder areas, duin/bos fire, the Spaarne, Noordzeekanaal, dense historic Haarlem, intense infrastructure dependence and cascading effects. These are regional qualitative/fictitious-scenario context, not validation of a GM0392 numeric probability or impact curve.

The crisis plan describes current multidisciplinary crisis-management processes, municipal bevolkingszorg, GHOR/GGD, police/fire/ambulance and partner coordination. The profile names neighbouring safety regions, water boards, Rijkswaterstaat and functional-chain partners. Plans describe roles and preparation, not event-time activation, resource availability, hospital acceptance, mutual aid, action completion or restoration.

The documents have regional/multi-year coverage, event-specific qualitative resolution and no explicit open-data reuse licence or machine update cadence found; the PDF carries VRK copyright. They are official context-only, not observed or operational feeds. Missing local detail is Unknown rather than proof of no risk or available capacity.

evidenceSources.title: Strategisch plan klimaatadaptatie, local heat/bridge operations and municipal open geodata
evidenceSources.edition: Strategic plan 2021 using the 2016 stress test; current heat and bridge pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted plan identifies water-nuisance locations at the Zijlweg rail underpass, centre streets, Rijksstraatweg and former watercourses; it says centre-adjacent districts are vulnerable, nearly all built-up districts can exceed 41°C perceived temperature, parks are cooler, and pre-1970 foundation areas around the centre are drought-sensitive. Its mapped planning analyses and reported incidents are not an observed current field or T+72 forecast.

Haarlem's 25 June 2026 notice temporarily stopped daytime movable-bridge operation for shipping because heat expansion could prevent safe closure; road traffic was kept on the closed bridges. The current heat page says some bridges are cooled with Spaarne water above 25°C. These source-dated operational examples prove heat/bridge coupling, not a permanent threshold, current incident, generic closure direction or future scenario state.

The city's current bridge page publishes named opening schedules and dated closures for the Spaarne Spoorbrug, Buitenrustbrug, Westelijke Randwegbrug and Waarderbrug, with the A9 Zijkanaal-C crossing in the coordinated standing-mast route. Schedules and project notices are not live passability, emergency priority or disaster throughput.

The plan does not state a native raster resolution, fixed refresh, blanket reuse licence or NoData encoding for its local stress maps. Haarlem exposes a public WMS/WFS root at https://data.haarlem.nl/, but layer-specific edition, licence and completeness must be verified before integration. Until then the stress maps remain source-dated context-only and missing areas remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland / Het Waterschapshuis / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: Rijnland boezem, Spaarndam controls, public water-system assets, national cloudburst scenario and Waterinfo
evidenceSources.edition: Rijnland current pages and 2025 legger inspected 3 September 2026; HWH/RWS deployment snapshots 2–3 September 2026; Klimaateffectatlas catalogue updated 5 August 2026; LIWO 2025.1.6
supports: Rijnland describes event-dependent pre-drawdown, full-capacity pumping, controlled emergency-pump deployment, peak storage, monitoring and kade inspection. Its Spaarndam page says Kolksluis, Woerdersluis, Boezemsluis and an IJdijk culvert are water-retaining works and that 2019 inspections found parts below current safety standards, with staged works continuing. Plans/works are context, not a current failure or live control state.

Rijnland's 2025 surface-water legger is queryable through an EPSG:28992 ArcGIS REST service returning JSON/GeoJSON and provides water location, required dimensions and maintenance responsibility; the authority says it updates the register regularly. No explicit layer reuse licence or fixed cadence was established on the service page, and design/register values are not observed level, capacity, telemetry, condition or performance.

The CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH IMWA/DAMO OGC snapshot assigns 51 point assets to GM0392: three sewer pumps, AWZI Haarlem-Waarderpolder, 43 surface-water pumps and four sluices. Contributor completeness varies; registration and gerealiseerd status do not prove connectivity, operation, spare capacity, power backup or repair. Unassigned/missing assets remain NoData.

LIWO deployment version 2025.1.6 exposes project deltares-rws/liwo/2025_0_1 with working scenario-information and water-depth tile generation. It is an irregular expert scenario catalogue, not a live forecast. Catalogue release, scenario/model dates, native resolution, source water body, defence/breach variant, depth bands, coverage and NoData must remain separate; a composite or available tile must never be inferred to be the selected Haarlem event.

The CC0 Rijkswaterstaat/Klimaateffectatlas WMS is a national modeled 70 mm in two hours scenario, with 0–10, 10–15, 15–20, 20–30 and over-30 cm classes; it is not a local stress test, current observation, forecast or selected incident and does not affect the model. Transparent/missing pixels remain Unknown. The Waterinfo snapshot has zero observations assigned within GM0392; generally ten-minute CC0 point observations are not a hydraulic surface and the absence is NoData, never zero level/discharge or safety.

evidenceSources.title: Observed weather, radar, warnings, seismic catalogue, air quality and combustible-nature context
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI observations valid 2 September 2026 23:30 UTC; radar valid 2 September 2026 15:50 UTC; warnings issued 2 September 2026 for 48 hours; RIVM observation 2 September 2026 17:00 UTC; IPO metadata updated 19 February 2026
supports: KNMI ten-minute station observations and five-minute national 1,024×1,024 radar rendering are CC BY 4.0, observed context-only and affectsSimulation=false. No station lies inside GM0392; nearest IJmuiden is 11.027 km away and reported wind/gust but no temperature or rain variables in the inspected record. Missing station variables and radar pixels/artifacts remain NoData and are never interpolated into neighbourhood forcing or T+72.

The continually updated CC BY 4.0 KNMI 48-hour warning product reported level 0 for Noord-Holland in its issued window. Zero means no issued warning for that window, not hazard-free conditions through T+72. The rolling FDSN catalogue contained no event assigned to Haarlem; absence of a matching event is not a seismic forecast, probability or licence to invent ground motion.

RIVM-Luchtmeetnet's Haarlem-Freddie Oversteegenstraat station reported indicative hourly PM2.5 3.39 µg/m³ at 17:00 UTC. The service states no standard reuse licence and values are local/revisable, not an exposure surface, source attribution, smoke plume or scenario-time forecast.

IPO/Risicokaart's Public Domain WMS, metadata updated 19 February 2026, maps eligible combustible forest/heath/dune areas with feature-scale accuracy and operational refresh cadence unstated. It is context-only—not ignition, fuel/moisture, perimeter, spread, smoke, evacuation or suppression—and missing geometry remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Gemeente Haarlem
evidenceSources.title: NWB roads, rail, scheduled transit, waterways/crossings and current transport notices
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail service inspected 3 September 2026; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; FIS-VNDS catalogue updated 15 April 2026; NDW published 2 September 2026 15:25 UTC
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB produces six logical GM0392 links: N205, A200 and N232 to Haarlemmermeer, N200 and N208 to Bloemendaal, and N208 to Velsen. The N208 edges share one physical corridor and are non-additive. Generalized 150/260 scenario-unit capacities are not observed vehicles, emergency access or freight throughput; the engine correctly restricts unqualified NWB edges to mobility and supply.

ProRail's manually updated CC0 OGC identifies Haarlem and Haarlem Spaarnwoude stations. OVapi GTFS version 9543, free-use best-effort data without an operational SLA, contains 164 stop areas. Static geometry and schedules do not prove event-time rail/bus operation, passenger capacity, accessibility, evacuation or restoration.

RWS FIS-VNDS is an April 2026 CC0 static waterway/bridge/lock register, not live navigation or operating state. Haarlem's public bridge pages and RWS vaarweginformatie provide record-specific schedules/notices, including dependency on the A9 Zijkanaal-C bridge outside GM0392. Roads, rail, waterways and movable crossings can be coupled but cannot be merged into one inferred availability value.

The CC0 NDW DATEX snapshot covers real/no-restriction records intersecting publication time through 72 hours; zero records were assigned to GM0392. Supplier records can be unvalidated and the snapshot is context-only. Zero matching records means no covered report, never that A9 approaches, A200/N200/N205/N208, city streets, tunnels, rail or bridges are open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Mijn Aansluiting / Liander / Netbeheer Nederland / PWN / RDI / RIVM / DUO / Register Externe Veiligheidsrisico's
evidenceSources.title: Public service territories, utility planning/register geometry, communications, acute care, education and industrial-risk context
evidenceSources.edition: Live provider queries 3 September 2026 with record updates September 2025–March 2026; public register snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The Public Domain live WMS/WFS point query identifies Liander electricity (record updated 24 March 2026), Liander gas (17 December 2025), PWN drinking water and Ziggo media (both 7 September 2025), but no drainage provider. These are point-sampled responsibility territories with provider-dependent refresh, not full municipal coverage, physical topology, quality, outage or restoration. Empty drainage remains NoData/Unknown.

Liander publishes CC BY 4.0 ArcGIS/WFS asset/register context and explicitly warns it does not replace KLIC or confer rights; its five-minute LianderPower research series covers anonymized 2013–2024 samples jittered up to 5 km and omits exact topology/switch state. NBNL's one-postcode Waarderpolder sample reports Liander planning values and 27 projects, with capacity/projects at least quarterly and queues monthly, exact dataset licence identifier not found. Neither product is live load, outage, emergency reserve or T+72 restoration.

RDI's statutory WFS returns 191 Haarlem antenna-installation records (90 mobile, 36 fixed link, three broadcast, six other mobile and 56 amateur), with service cadence and reuse licence unstated. Installation points do not prove radio coverage, ownership, traffic, backhaul, power/backup, availability or restoration.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 (CC0, national 2026 questionnaire) reports Spaarne Gasthuis Haarlem with 19 treatment rooms, 26,768 visits in 2025, 24/7 SEH and acute obstetrics; Spaarne Gasthuis Hoofddorp is about 6.1 km away and reports 14 rooms and 18,801 visits. DUO daily CC-BY-with-version-unspecified data returns 115 education-use locations. These are dated facility/register facts, not live occupancy, shelter role, acceptance/diversion, staffing, generator endurance, supplies or access.

REV public WMS depicts regulated fire/explosion/toxic, pipeline and Basisnet attention areas; fixed snapshot cadence, record-valid time and reuse licence were not stated by the service. It is risk-source context, not a current industrial incident, release rate, plume or control state. Missing objects never prove zero risk. All listed public layers remain affectsSimulation=false absent a reviewed causal adapter.

evidenceSources.title: National first-72-hour household preparedness guidance
supports: National guidance recommends supplies for 72 hours, including three litres of water per person per day, food, radio, power bank and medicines. Rijksoverheid material is CC0 unless otherwise indicated, but this is national public information without operational refresh, spatial resolution below household/self-report, event-valid state or municipal measurement.

Denk Vooruit explains that crises can last longer and emergency services cannot be everywhere immediately. The advice is planning context, not measured Haarlem preparedness, guaranteed aid arrival, a resource inventory or recovery deadline.

Household stocks, reception/distribution capacity, opened facilities, mutual aid, crews, vehicles, fuel, spares, medicines and completed actions remain Unknown until time-stamped authoritative state is supplied.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline population agree.
notes: Manifest, generated collection and model uniquely identify GM0392 as Haarlem in Noord-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Kennemerland.
BoundaryEdition and statisticsEdition are 2025. Current 2026 observations/notices, older stress tests, multi-year plans/registers and synthetic scenario time retain distinct semantics.
No identity, centre-containment, province, safety-region or headline-population contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Full and generalized 2025 municipal geometry are topologically coherent and contain the official place labels.
notes: The full and generalized municipality are each a one-component, one-ring MultiPolygon; simplification from 1,654 to 95 vertices retains overview topology. There is no detached 2025 component to restore.
Both BAG place labels fall inside the generalized boundary. BRT's Haarlem and Zuid Schalkwijk categories differ from BAG's Haarlem and Spaarndam gem. Haarlem because of dataset purpose and scale.
Administrative containment is not hydraulic connectivity, defence compartment, sewer catchment, fire fuel, industrial plume, route passability or utility service area.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and rounded neighbourhood populations reconcile without inventing values.
notes: Official/generated population is 168,743, density 5,776/km², age65Pct 17.6 and one-person households 35,803.
Published neighbourhoods sum to 168,770, 27 above the municipal total (+0.016%); deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 168,743.

Largest published neighbourhoods are Binnenstad 3,435, Vijfhoek 3,390, Koninginnebuurt 2,910, Kleverpark-noord 2,835 and Stedenbuurt-west 2,800. These counts omit transient demand and do not reveal medical dependency or household stocks.

regionalDetail.summary: All 111 neighbourhoods load, but several CBS attributes and every operational hazard/lifeline field remain incomplete.
notes: Core population/age/business/car/home/household fields cover 111/111; address density/urbanity cover 110, home value 96, household size/doctor/supermarket/density 106, cars per household 94, and benefit/housing percentage fields 97. District heating and public charging cover 0/111 and remain NoData.
Local stress plans, 51 water assets, 191 antennas, one hospital, 115 education records and one grid-planning sample add context but no complete event-time operational layer.
NoData masks, denominators, edition/time, uncertainty, coverage and affectsSimulation must remain visible at neighbourhood scale.

settlements.summary: BAG and BRT settlement data are internally coherent and correctly retained as contextual labels.
notes: Two active BAG woonplaats labels and two BRT settlement features are represented with no out-of-boundary label-point flag.
Spaarndam gem. Haarlem and Zuid Schalkwijk illustrate register/cartographic classification differences, not missing population or services.
Settlement labels cannot establish incident occupancy, isolation, utility connection, shelter/reception role or evacuation throughput.

transport.summary: Public road, rail, transit and waterway context is reproducible, but Haarlem's crossings and cross-boundary access lack event-valid state and capacity.
notes: Six NWB links cover A200/N200/N205/N208/N232 toward Haarlemmermeer, Bloemendaal and Velsen; N208 is one shared corridor. Nearby A9 dependence is reached only through neighbouring municipalities and the Zijkanaal-C crossing is not an independent Haarlem capacity edge.

Two stations and 164 stops are static schedule/geometry context. Movable Spaarne bridges, rail bridges/tunnels and regional approaches have weather, works and navigation dependencies that are not joined to scenario time.

Zero assigned NDW records is NoData for unreported roads, not proof that A9 approaches, A200/N200/N205/N208, tunnels, rail or bridges are open. Hospital access, patient diversion and mutual-aid/supply throughput remain Unknown.

emergencyContext.summary: Official roles, care/register points and 72-hour guidance exist, but actions and resources are not auditable scenario state.
notes: VRK distinguishes regional crisis management, municipality bevolkingszorg and functional-chain authority, with cross-region and operator coordination. Plans do not prove activation, staffing or completion.

Spaarne Gasthuis Haarlem/Hoofddorp and education locations do not establish live occupants, facility opening, acceptance/diversion, routes, staff, power/water backup, fuel, medicine or shelter/distribution roles.
The national 72-hour recommendation is not measured preparedness, an aid-delivery promise or a recovery deadline.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All nine individual hazards plus compound produce complete finite deterministic results at six checkpoints for eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: The gate executed severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

T+24 severity / affected people-equivalent / cumulative local pre-network event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.166109 / 52,229 / 834,356.23; pluvial 0.379909 / 37,409 / 725,483.05; river 0 / 0 / 0; coastal 0.660300 / 99,044 / 1,700,222.55; heat 0.094058 / 11,509 / 400,161.13.

These are deterministic scenario proxies. Affected people-equivalent is not identified residents/customers, and person-hours is cumulative matched-baseline weighted local pre-network service shortfall—not casualties, displacement, economic loss or an operator report.

numericalInvariants.summary: Deterministic, finite, bounded, reconciliation, counterfactual and monotonic-burden contracts pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0392 pnpm audit:model passes both current municipality-coverage tests.

All 111 local rows reconcile exactly to 168,743 residents and municipal demand/delivery; no-event attribution is zero, repeated output is deterministic, service-layer selection leaves physical hazard invariant and cumulative person-hours is monotonic.
Passing arithmetic contracts does not calibrate local hazard, exposure, topology, response or restoration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse one full neighbourhood order, and controlled earthquake/fire sources fail containment plausibility.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have exactly the same full 111-neighbourhood order, led by Romolenpolder-west (25 residents), Tuinbouwgebied-noord (45), Van Aemstelbuurt, Ramplaankwartier and zero-resident Oude Spaarndammerpolder. River and canonical earthquake are all-zero ties at that checkpoint.

A controlled earthquake source at the municipal centre lies in BU03920104 Burgwal but the containing neighbourhood ranks 99/111 at T+6 while modeled ground motion is 0.179801 g. A controlled wildfire source at the centre of BU03920207 Haarlemmerhout ranks its containing neighbourhood 97/111 at T+24 while direct fire is 0.661411 and smoke 0.565095.

The controlled sources test geometry/allocation only and do not assert real incidents. E03's centre/Zijlweg/Rijksstraatweg/heat patterns and E04's water pathways independently contradict a universal random order.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service ledgers are inspectable but precise dependencies are not calibrated to Haarlem's physical utilities, water controls, crossings or facilities.
notes: The current source=NWB rule correctly limits public roads to mobility and supply and keeps routes logical/non-additive. The six edges still do not encode live city access, bridge/tunnel state, emergency priority or observed throughput.

Public provider territories, Liander register geometry, NBNL planning, water assets, antennas and facility records stay affectsSimulation=false. They do not validate exact availability, demand, reserve, dependency coefficients, backup or recovery.

Rijnland's operational options demonstrate weather–boezem–pump–storage–kade coupling, but no live state/setpoint/capacity/backup/repair feed is bound. Wastewater, surface water and drinking-water quantity/pressure/quality require distinct causal state.

causalTrace.summary: Generic evidence and NoData semantics are visible, but exact Haarlem outputs lack a persistent municipality-specific evidence-gap contract.
notes: Desktop 1440×1000 and mobile 375×812 checks had no horizontal overflow or browser errors; mobile Tune, hazard layer, timeline and Details controls were reachable.

At coastal T+24 both viewports showed Haarlem '100% inundation stress' and 'Scenario · evidence class derived-screening'; aria-live announced 'Haarlem: 66% scenario severity.' The inspector correctly says Haarlem has zero Waterinfo observations and that this means NoData, and identifies nearest KNMI IJmuiden with missing temperature/rain.

No adjacent Haarlem-specific warning states that coastal/Noordzeekanaal/Spaarne boundary condition, defence/breach/control state, connected footprint, arrival/recession and utility calibration are absent. Generic evidence class alone does not qualify exact affected/service/recovery values.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 service recovery and compound persistence are deterministic but not caused by Haarlem actions, hydraulic state, access or resources.
notes: Coastal direct forcing is zero at T+72 but 10,015 people-equivalent remain affected, cumulative burden reaches 5,051,526.79 person-hours and status is recovering. No selected hydrograph, defence/control state, recession/dewatering, inspection, access or operator action supports the trajectory.

Compound T+72 retains internal flood amplitude 0.544681, severity 0.531944, 109,761 affected and 5,925,750.30 person-hours. Availability is power 0.377401, water 0.423442, drainage 0.320375, gas 0.573628, telecom 0.287706, mobility 0.500036, facilities 0.373157 and supply 0.357000.

No time-stamped warning, evacuation, reception, hospital diversion, temporary water, pump/control action, switching, bridge/traffic measure, repair, distribution or mutual-aid ledger supports these values. Seventy-two hours is a planning horizon rather than a guaranteed aid or restoration time.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated nonzero individual hazards use exactly the same full 111-neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire at T+24 are all led by Romolenpolder-west, Tuinbouwgebied-noord, Van Aemstelbuurt, Ramplaankwartier and Oude Spaarndammerpolder. E03 instead identifies centre, Zijlweg, Rijksstraatweg, former waterways, low-green districts, parks and bridge heat; E04 supplies separate water geometry. One shared seeded order cannot represent all mechanisms.
findings.action: Replace the common local seed with source/coverage-aware hazard-family adapters and assert that unrelated hazards cannot share a complete order unless identical source evidence explicitly justifies it. Missing local cells remain Unknown rather than pseudo-precise.

findings.summary: Controlled earthquake and wildfire sources do not prioritize their containing Haarlem neighbourhoods.
findings.evidence: At T+6 a controlled source at the municipal centre is inside Burgwal but Burgwal ranks 99/111 while groundMotionG is 0.179801. At T+24 a controlled source at the Haarlemmerhout neighbourhood centre is inside Haarlemmerhout but ranks 97/111 with fire 0.661411 and smoke 0.565095. These synthetic controls test source allocation, not incident truth.
findings.action: Enforce distance/containment for source-driven direct effects, with separate earthquake site/exposure and fire fuel/wind/barrier/access/suppression paths. Add controlled fixtures for containing and adjacent neighbourhoods; keep unsupported real-event outputs Unknown.

findings.summary: Coastal flooding is over-precise while the major-river zero does not cover Haarlem's actual water pathways.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+24 has legacy internal flood amplitude 2.129932, rendered as 100% inundation stress, severity 0.660300, 99,044 affected and 1,700,222.55 person-hours without a selected source water body, hydrograph/datum, coastal/Noordzeekanaal/Spaarne defence or control state, footprint, arrival or recession. River remains exact zero. E02–E04 establish coastal/regional-kade, Spaarne/Rijnland boezem, polder and pluvial pathways that neither result causally represents.
findings.action: Retain the river zero only as a narrowly labelled Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct-network exclusion; never present it as an all-clear for Spaarne/Rijnland water. Retain coastal output only as an internal proximity diagnostic, suppress local severity/affected/recovery claims until an authority-selected LIWO/Rijnland event preserves event, defence/control, footprint, units, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData.

findings.summary: Haarlem's known rain pathways and water controls do not drive pluvial allocation or drainage causality.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 uses the universal order and leads with Romolenpolder-west/Tuinbouwgebied-noord, while the official plan identifies centre-adjacent districts, the Zijlweg underpass, Rijksstraatweg and former watercourses. The public bundle has 51 water assets and a national 70 mm/two-hour layer, but these remain non-causal; exact drainage availability 0.526853 at T+12/T+24 lacks sewer/catchment topology, storage, controls, live operation, power backup and emptying time.
findings.action: Acquire an authorized local stress-test/catchment/control-zone export and bind a selected rainfall duration. Preserve CRS, cells/classes, units, edition, licence, coverage and NoData; separate municipal sewer, Rijnland surface water, AWZI and drinking-water state. Asset geometry stays context-only until connectivity and operation are reviewed.

findings.summary: Storm, heat, winter, remote earthquake/fire and cyber outputs are scenario proxies without event-valid local forcing or target state.
findings.evidence: Nearest KNMI station IJmuiden is outside Haarlem and lacks temperature/rain in the snapshot; warning level zero covers only the issued 48 hours. Yet winter T+24 generates 26.644 m/s wind, -8.556°C, 4.484 cm/h snow and 0.750 ice; heat uses the same spatial order despite Haarlem's park/built-form evidence. The Groningen earthquake produces 0.004030 g at T+6 without an event/ShakeMap; remote wildfire has zero local flame but 0.305987 smoke; cyber names no target/path.
findings.action: Keep named preset geography and synthetic evidence explicit. Suppress engineering g and locally predictive weather/smoke claims absent selected event-valid KNMI/ShakeMap/plume inputs. Use local land-cover/vulnerability for heat/fire; a cyber exercise needs a named aggregate target, attack/containment state and operator-approved dependency contract.

findings.summary: Public utility data provides useful responsibility and planning context but not safe physical topology or live service state.
findings.evidence: E04/E07 identify Liander/PWN/Ziggo territories, one NBNL planning sample, public Liander geometry, 51 water assets, 191 antenna records and facilities. Their coverage and cadence differ and none proves exact feeder/pipe/sewer/backhaul connectivity, switching, load/pressure/quality/coverage, backup, crew or restoration. The empty drainage-provider lookup is incomplete, not absence.
findings.action: Keep affectsSimulation=false and explicit edition, cadence, resolution, coverage, licence and NoData. Use only operator-authorized security-reviewed aggregate zones for causal utility modeling; otherwise use visibly synthetic values and never claim physical topology.

findings.summary: Logical road/rail links omit event-valid bridge, tunnel, A9 approach, hospital and mutual-aid capacity.
findings.evidence: Six logical links, two stations and 164 stops are static. E03/E06 show heat and works can change movable-bridge/rail/tunnel and navigation state and that A9 Zijkanaal-C participates in the through route outside GM0392. Spaarne Gasthuis Haarlem and nearby Hoofddorp are registered, but no route passability, ambulance priority, acceptance/diversion, staffing or cross-boundary aid/supply throughput is ingested. Zero NDW matches is not open-road evidence.
findings.action: Add source-dated multimodal corridor/crossing state with direction, common-corridor identity, issue/valid/expiry time, passability, emergency priority, capacity units, confidence and source. Hospital acceptance, diversion, mutual aid and essential supplies remain Unknown until authority-confirmed.

findings.summary: Exact T+72 recovery and compound service values lack accountable actions and resources.
findings.evidence: Coastal T+72 has zero direct forcing but 10,015 affected and 5,051,526.79 person-hours. Compound T+72 retains 109,761 affected and exact availability power 0.377401, water 0.423442, drainage 0.320375, gas 0.573628, telecom 0.287706, mobility 0.500036, facilities 0.373157 and supply 0.357000. Plans/guidance do not supply executed warnings, evacuations, reception, hospital diversion, pumps, switching, bridge control, repairs, distribution, mutual aid, crews, fuel or spares.
findings.action: Add an intervention/resource ledger with authority, trigger/units, proposed/requested/confirmed/started/completed/failed/cancelled status, issue/valid/expiry time, capacity, resources, dependencies, confidence and source. Do not convert preparedness plans or 72-hour guidance into completed actions or recovery.

findings.summary: Industrial/hazardous-substance risks documented for Kennemerland are outside the canonical incident set.

residualLimitations: This deterministic planning audit is not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, Rijnland, VRK, Haarlem, hospital or utility forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate, damage assessment or restoration commitment.

The 2025 municipality is a single-component MultiPolygon. Generalized CBS neighbourhoods and BAG/BRT labels are overview geography, not sewer catchments, water/defence compartments, fire fuels, industrial plumes, route access or utility topology.

The legacy coastal amplitude is rendered as normalized inundation stress, not metres. No selected North-Sea/Noordzeekanaal/Spaarne hydrograph/datum, defence/breach/control state, connected footprint, arrival/recession or NoData mask drives Haarlem.

The exact-zero river screen excludes only direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel proximity. It says nothing about the Spaarne, Rijnland boezem, regional kades, polders, groundwater, sewers or pluvial water and must not be an all-clear.

Haarlem's local stress evidence is planning/model context and the national 70 mm/two-hour raster is a separate scenario. Neither is sampled into current neighbourhood forcing; transparent/missing coverage remains Unknown.

Rijnland legger and HWH assets describe registers/design/locations, not complete connectivity, live level/flow, setpoints, condition, capacity, backup, failure or repair. Zero Haarlem Waterinfo points is NoData.

KNMI points/radar/warnings retain distinct valid times and do not drive the scenario. Nearest IJmuiden missing variables remain NoData; warning zero covers only the issued window. Earthquake g and smoke are not supported by a selected event/ShakeMap or plume.

NWB, ProRail, GTFS and FIS-VNDS are static geometry/schedule/register context. NDW absence does not establish passability, and there is no complete event-time A9/A200/N200/N205/N208, bridge, tunnel, rail or waterway state.

No complete safe public source supplies Liander feeder/switch topology, PWN pipe/pressure/quality, municipal sewer connectivity, Rijnland controls, telecom backhaul, facility dependencies, live stocks, backups, crews or restoration. Sensitive details were not inferred.

Provider territories, NBNL planning, RDI antennas, RIVM/DUO facilities and REV objects are context with distinct coverage/time. They do not establish service, shelter, care acceptance, industrial release or incident state.

Registered residents omit visitors, commuters, patients, students registered elsewhere and responders. Household readiness, medical dependency, facility occupants, reception, mutual aid, water/food/medicine/fuel, staff, vehicles and repair priorities remain assumed or Unknown.

Affected people-equivalent and pressure are model proxies; deprived person-hours is cumulative local pre-network matched-baseline weighted service shortfall. Neither equals identified customers, casualties, displacement, welfare loss or economic damage, and six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid rainfall, wind, traffic, bridge and control changes.
